papers.title: When Sinks Help or Hurt: Unified Framework for Attention Sink in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.paper_type: Large Vision-Language Model / Attention Sink / Multimodal method paper
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes attention sinks in large vision-language models by separating visual sinks that propagate from the vision encoder from sinks that emerge in the language model. It studies when these sinks help global reasoning and when they suppress fine-grained visual evidence, and introduces a lightweight layer-wise gating method.

papers.title: Losing Visual Needles in Image Haystacks: Vision Language Models are Easily Distracted in Short and Long Contexts
papers.paper_type: Vision-Language Model / Long Visual Context / Evaluation benchmark paper
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LoCoVQA, a benchmark for testing whether vision-language models can answer questions while ignoring distracting visual context. It evaluates short and long visual contexts and shows that many VLMs lose accuracy as irrelevant images are added.

papers.title: Long Context Transfer from Language to Vision
papers.paper_type: Large Multimodal Model / Long Context / Video Understanding method paper
papers.abstract: This paper studies how long-context capability learned by a language backbone can transfer to visual and video inputs. It presents LongVA, a large multimodal model that extends context length for long video understanding without requiring dense long-video supervised training.

papers.title: Vision Transformers Don't Need Trained Registers
papers.paper_type: Vision Transformer / Registers / Training-free method paper
papers.abstract: This paper investigates high-norm outlier tokens in Vision Transformers and proposes a training-free test-time register approach. It shifts selected activations into an untrained token to reduce artifacts, clean up attention or feature maps, and improve downstream visual tasks.
